prompt.reply.title: How to write your reply
prompt.reply.box: Your reply appears in a small text box, one line at a time, and {player} clicks through it. Write for that:
prompt.reply.lectureLines: - This reply opens the class with the lecture: write {lines} lines, each on its own line. Each line is one beat.
prompt.reply.lines: - Write {lines} short lines, each on its own line. Each line is one beat.

prompt.reply.words: - Keep every line under {lineWords} words, and the whole reply under {words}.
prompt.reply.speaker: - {speaker} is teaching the class and has a voice in the scene: a line of theirs starts with "{speaker}:".
prompt.reply.noCalling: - {speaker} teaches the room and does not call on {player}, put a question to him or single him out. A question asked of the class is answered by another student: one of you, or someone unnamed in a line of narration. Only when {player} himself speaks to {speaker}, or puts his hand up, does {speaker} answer him directly.
prompt.reply.named: - Most lines are speech. Start every spoken line with the speaker's first name and a colon, then what they say, with no quotation marks: {firstName}: Sit down, then.
prompt.reply.plain: - Most lines are things you say, written plainly with no quotation marks.
prompt.reply.group: - Not everyone speaks every time. Let whoever would naturally answer speak; {others} should each get a line now and then, and may talk to each other.
prompt.reply.lectureNarration: - A line of narration is written in the third person and present tense, between asterisks: *The room settles.*
prompt.reply.namedAction: - At most one line may be a small action by one of you, naming them, in the third person and present tense, between asterisks: *Ana glances at the door.*
prompt.reply.action: - At most one line may be a small action or expression of your own, in the third person and present tense, between asterisks: *She glances at the door.*
prompt.reply.lectureNever: - Never write what {player} says, does or feels.
prompt.reply.never: - Never describe the scenery, and never write what {player} says, does or feels.
prompt.reply.end: - Say one thing and stop. End on something {player} can answer. This is a conversation, not a speech: short turns, back and forth.
prompt.reply.unknowable: - {player} knows only what he has seen or been told. Anything you invent (a book's contents, a person, an event he wasn't at) he cannot know: tell him about it rather than ask him about it, and ask him only about himself, his opinions, and what has happened in front of him.

memory.core: - "{level}": a moment that defines what she and {player} are to each other, which she will carry for good: a first kiss, the first time they slept together, a confession, a promise made or broken, a real fight or a betrayal, something she had never told anyone. Rare.

memory.amounts: - 0: nothing changed. 1 to 2: a pleasant time, a small kindness, a good laugh. 3 to 5: he really reached her, or something happened between them. 6 to 10: rare, a moment she will come back to for weeks.
memory.negative: - Negative when he bored her, ignored her, pushed when she was uneasy, embarrassed or insulted her, broke a promise or showed her something she dislikes in him; as far down as he earned.
memory.three: - The three move on their own. Affection is fondness and warmth. Trust is whether she can rely on him and be honest with him: kept words, discretion, not being pressed. Desire is wanting him: it rises with attraction and tension, and can rise while trust falls.
memory.admires: - What she admires in a man tilts all of it: where {player} has it she warms to the same behaviour sooner, and where he lacks it he has more to prove.
memory.reason: - "{key}": one short sentence, in the third person, on why it moved as it did.
memory.sex: - "{key}": true only if {name} and {player} had sex with each other in this scene, of any kind; false for kissing, flirting, talk of it, or sex that involved only others.
memory.learned: - "{key}": the ids of the things below that {player} found out about {name} in this scene, because she plainly said or showed them; [] when none did. Only ids from this list, and only what really came out:
memory.rapport: - "{key}": how {name} stands with any of the others where this scene truly changed it from how they stood before (said below): a quarrel that will not be forgotten, a peace made, a friendship struck up. Not for a passing mood or one sharp remark; [] when nothing changed. Each entry: "{withKey}" is one of {ids}, and "{relationKey}" is one of {relations}.
memory.drawnTo: - She is drawn to {admires} in a man. {appeal}
memory.ordinary: {player} is ordinary in that so far.
memory.stage: - With {player} she is at the stage "{stage}": affection {affection}, trust {trust}, desire {desire}, each of {max}.
memory.before: - Before this scene she and {other} were {relation, select, friends {friends} enemies {enemies} other {neither friends nor enemies}}.
memory.comfort: - By the end she put how much she wanted to be there at {level} of 5{why, select, true {: {reason}} other {}}.
spending.task: You keep the accounts of a dating sim. Given what was said in one scene, work out what {player} himself paid for in it, and what it came to.
spending.json: Reply with only a JSON object and nothing else: {shape}
spending.count: - Count only what {player} plainly paid for or said he would: "the drinks are on me", buying a round, paying for dinner, tickets, a cab, something bought for someone. What someone else paid for, what was free, what was only talked about, and what he was given are not his.
spending.price: - "{spent}" is a whole number of dollars, with no $ sign. Price it as it would be priced in the United States: a coffee or a tea $4 to $6, a drink at a bar $8 to $12, a casual meal for one $15 to $25, a good dinner for two $80 to $150. Count each person he paid for.
spending.nothing: - If he paid for nothing, "{spent}" is 0 and "{on}" is empty. Most scenes cost nothing; do not look for a reason to charge him.
spending.on: - "{on}" says what it went on in a few words, with the place when there is one: "drinks for two at Boba Blossom".
spending.gifts: - Gifts he handed over were paid for when he bought them: leave them out ({gifts}).
spending.shift: - He is at work in this scene: what he serves or sells as part of the job is not his money.

relics.moment.unravel: Every stitch of clothing on everyone here, {player} included, has just vanished into thin air. Nobody knows why; react in surprise.
relics.moment.stillness: Time has just stopped for everyone here but {player} and you: everyone else is frozen where they stand, and will see and hear nothing. You do not know why.
relics.moment.sapphic: A charm has just settled over the women here: you feel drawn to each other, and want to kiss. You do not know why.
relics.moment.firstSeed: A warmth spreads low in every woman here: the Bloom is wide open in her tonight. You do not know why.

masquerade.noSex: This is a dance on a crowded ballroom floor: flirt, tease and dance, but start no sex-act and use no {tag} tag.
masquerade.arrival: A woman in {mask} comes out of the crowd of dancers and holds out a gloved hand to you.
masquerade.arrivalBare: Through the masks and gowns comes someone wearing a mask and nothing else at all, waving at you.
masquerade.secret: You are wearing {description}. The mask is enchanted: nobody can tell who is under it, not by face, figure, hair or voice. You have come to dance with {player} without his knowing it is you, and you keep it secret: never say your name, nor anything that gives it away outright, and in narration you are "the Lady in {mask}". In every other way you are yourself, in how you talk, tease and move, so that he might guess. If he guesses, neither confirm nor deny it. One dance, and you slip back into the crowd.
masquerade.secretBare: You have come to the masquerade as you always are: in nothing but a mask, which hides nobody. Dance with {player}, and enjoy the stir you cause.
masquerade.notKnown: He did not know her under her mask.
masquerade.named: You say her name. The Lady in {mask} goes still, then laughs, takes your hand, and leads you out through the glass doors onto the moonlit terrace.
masquerade.terrace: It is the end of {event}. {player} saw through your enchanted mask and named you, and you are glad to be found out. You are still in {description}. You lead him out onto the terrace, away from the ball, and make love to him there in your gown and mask: on your knees with him in your mouth, bent over the stone balustrade with your skirt hiked up, on the garden bench with your skirt hiked up, and at the last him finishing inside you.
viewing.title: Viewing of {house}
viewing.description: {officer} has walked you through {house} room by room, keys in hand, and brings you back to the hearth room, where the nanny is waiting to meet you.
viewing.direction: This is the hour {player} is given {house}. {officer}, the housing officer of the Sire Relations Office, has just shown him round it: which rooms are furnished, which stand bare for him to build, where the wards are, and the terms of the rent. She has introduced you, the nanny who lives in the house, and you have told him how the children are looked after here and what makes a child thrive. You are meeting {player} for the first time, in what is now his home and yours. {officer} is here and speaks for herself, exact and brief, and leaves once his questions are answered. Stay in the house: do not move the scene anywhere.
